page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance belonging to the memory-optimized server family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, backed by vector extensions including AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) alongside AES cryptographic instructions. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 0 GPUs, no bundled local storage, and a baseline network bandwidth limit of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results for the ecs.re6p.2xlarge illustrate consistent middle-tier performance across general compute and memory workflows, contrasted by limitations in single-core throughput. In PassMark testing, the instance achieved an overall CPU score of 8301.57, an extended instructions score of 6404.96, and a memory score of 2296.82, all placing within the average category. Geekbench metrics align closely, posting a multi-core score of 4501.0 and a single-core score of 1168.0, with subtests like Clang compilation scoring 6636.0 and ray tracing reaching 5655.0. However, raw compute density falls behind modern architectures in specific scenarios, evidenced by weak bottom-quartile ratings in stress-ng single-core performance (1317.89), single-threaded gzip compression (22.74 GB/sec), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (34.61 GB/sec), and Geekbench image processing (3916.0).

Memory subsystem throughput remains reliable for enterprise workloads, measuring 392.37 GB/sec for small-block cached read operations, 50.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 37.46 GB/sec for large-block writes. In operational application benchmarks, the instance recorded 6.88 million operations per second in Redis SET throughput and maintained 6.75 GB/sec in static web serving, both falling within the middle 50% distribution. Given the absence of local storage, storage-bound workloads depend entirely on external network-attached volumes, bounded by the 2 Gbps network baseline. The ecs.re6p.2xlarge serves as a balanced mid-range environment best suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, moderate database operations, and multi-threaded enterprise web serving where dedicated core allocation is required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p.2xlarge is a memory-optimized KVM-based virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core), 32.0 GB of system RAM, AVX-512 support, and a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance operates without bundled local storage or GPUs, utilizing a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results position the server solidly in the mid-range for memory bandwidth (50.74 GB/sec large block read), Redis SET throughput (6.88 million ops/sec), and multi-core Geekbench performance (4501.0), although single-core throughput and compression speeds fall into the lower quartile. Without local NVMe disks, disk persistence relies on remote block storage. It is suitable for in-memory caching, moderate databases, and standard multi-threaded web backend services.
